note: Melody ranges from the Singing Carrots song database (singingcarrots.com, user-submitted). Vocal Lab checks the real notes once a song is added.

musicianwave.name: Musician Wave: 50 easy songs to sing

emastered.name: eMastered: 30 easy songs for beginner singers

30daysinger.name: 30 Day Singer: best karaoke songs for low voices

zinginstruments.name: Zing Instruments: 17 easy songs to sing

levels.easy: About an octave or less, slow or steady tempo, small steps, a repeating chorus.
levels.medium: Wider span or a jump into the chorus, faster or wordier lines, long held phrases.
levels.hard: Fast, dense lyrics, tricky timing or key changes, or the whole of your range with exposed held notes.

songs.title: Riders on the Storm
songs.why: Low, slow and repetitive; almost every line sits on the same few notes.

songs.title: Walk on the Wild Side
songs.why: Half-spoken verses over one octave; the "doo, da-doo" hook is the only real tune.

songs.title: Hurt
songs.why: Slow, close to speech, and low; the work is keeping the long notes steady.

songs.title: Budapest
songs.why: One octave, a bouncy repeated chorus and no leaps.

songs.title: Love Me Tender
songs.why: Slow, stepwise melody; good for practising smooth, held notes.

songs.title: In the Ghetto
songs.why: Storytelling verses on a narrow tune; the chorus repeats the verse shape.

songs.title: Make You Feel My Love
songs.why: Slow ballad, small steps, lots of space to breathe between lines.

songs.title: Blowin' in the Wind
songs.why: Under an octave, folk-simple, same tune every verse.

songs.title: Mad World
songs.why: Slow, quiet and narrow; mostly a few repeated notes.

songs.title: Under the Milky Way
songs.why: One octave in a relaxed baritone; the chorus repeats.

songs.title: The Passenger
songs.why: Under an octave, steady rhythm, and a "la la la" chorus.

songs.title: Love Will Tear Us Apart
songs.why: Low, narrow and repetitive; mostly about rhythm.

songs.title: Chasing Cars
songs.why: Under an octave and nearly spoken in the verses.

songs.title: Fields of Gold
songs.why: One octave, slow, smooth lines.

songs.title: Losing My Religion
songs.why: Built around a single note with small jumps.

songs.title: From Little Things Big Things Grow
songs.why: One octave, a story told over the same simple verse tune.

songs.title: A Horse with No Name
songs.why: Two chords, a tiny range and a "la la" chorus.

songs.title: Lucille
songs.why: Narrow and conversational; the chorus is the easiest part.

songs.title: Forever and Ever, Amen
songs.why: Low country baritone, narrow and repetitive.

songs.title: Always on My Mind
songs.why: Slow, gentle, small range; good for soft singing.

songs.title: Better Together
songs.why: Laid-back, quiet, mostly stepwise.

songs.title: Boulevard of Broken Dreams
songs.why: One octave and a steady beat; the chorus repeats.

songs.title: Wonderful Tonight
songs.why: Slow and simple; good for long, even notes.

songs.title: Duncan
songs.why: Pub sing-along: one octave, four lines, round and round.

songs.title: Folsom Prison Blues
songs.why: Uses your whole range, bottom note to top, at a brisk shuffle.

songs.title: Ghost Riders in the Sky
songs.why: Sits right on your lowest notes; the "yippie-yi-ay" needs a steady, full tone.

songs.title: Red Right Hand
songs.why: Range is small, but the tone and timing are hard to nail.

songs.title: Dumb Things
songs.why: Quick, wordy lines over a wider range.

songs.title: How to Make Gravy
songs.why: Long, talky verses that climb in the chorus.

songs.title: No Aphrodisiac
songs.why: Long song with lots of words and a build to the top of the range.

songs.title: Lean on Me
songs.why: Simple tune but a wide span, and the "call me" lines move fast.

songs.title: Strangers in the Night
songs.why: Long, held crooner phrases; breath control matters.

songs.title: The Gambler
songs.why: Story verses then a chorus that jumps up.

songs.title: Copperhead Road
songs.why: Lots of words, half-shouted, at a driving tempo.

songs.title: Sixteen Tons
songs.why: Deep, round tone across a wide span; swing timing.

songs.title: Proud Mary
songs.why: Gritty rock voice and a jump into the chorus.

songs.title: Wild World
songs.why: Chorus climbs, with a held top note.

songs.title: If You Could Read My Mind
songs.why: Narrow, but very long lines with few places to breathe.

songs.title: Brothers in Arms
songs.why: Very low, slow and quiet; your bottom notes need to stay in tune.

songs.title: The Man Who Sold the World
songs.why: Unplugged version; odd intervals and a held top note.

songs.title: Should I Stay or Should I Go
songs.why: Shouty energy and quick switches between verse and chorus.

songs.title: Day-O (The Banana Boat Song)
songs.why: Long called-out "Day-O" notes and call-and-answer timing.

songs.title: Just Breathe
songs.why: Gentle, but covers almost your whole range.

songs.title: Time in a Bottle
songs.why: Lilting 3/4 melody with jumps and long phrases.

songs.title: Everybody Knows
songs.why: Low, wordy and steady; holding pitch while half-speaking is the skill.

songs.title: I've Been Everywhere
songs.why: Narrow range but a rapid list of place names: breath and diction at speed.

songs.title: One Week
songs.why: Rap-speed verses on your lowest notes, then a sung chorus.

songs.title: Subterranean Homesick Blues
songs.why: Non-stop fast lyrics with almost nowhere to breathe.

songs.title: Sultans of Swing
songs.why: Long, dense verses over a wide span, sung against a busy band.

songs.title: Mack the Knife
songs.why: Swing timing and a key change up a step every verse.

songs.title: Mmm Mmm Mmm Mmm
songs.why: Long humming notes deep in your range; very demanding for a low voice.

songs.title: Perfect Day
songs.why: Soft low verses, then a climb to your top notes in the "reap" section.

songs.title: Fire and Rain
songs.why: Uses your whole range, with long, exposed held notes.
